purpose: Assess utility of editable Lecturer drafts; semantic errors are recorded and corrected, not an early-stop gate. This is a new user-authorized continuation, not a successful prior B gate.
sample_change: Original preplanned valid solution texts unchanged except a fictional Author header for anonymity testing; no real person data.

conditional-update.atomicity_rollback: Both writes in one transaction, commit together; explicit rollback undoes both on failure. Correct, no mandatory atomicity keyword.
conditional-update.duplicate_vs_capacity: Explicit unique pair protects same-student duplicates, not cross-student capacity. Correct.
conditional-update.capacity: Atomic positive-count conditional decrement, enrollment accepted only on success; later insert failure rolls back. Correct. Row lock is not additionally required.
conditional-update.cache: Display/read speed, possible stale data, cached result never authorizes; database reservation authoritative. Correct.

locked-recheck.atomicity_rollback: One transaction holds lock, commits both updates; either write failure rolls back all. Correct.
locked-recheck.duplicate_vs_capacity: Unique pair handles repeat student; lock handles capacity across students. Correct.
locked-recheck.capacity: Exclusive shared course-row lock, check after acquiring, decrement/insert before releasing; next request waits and rechecks. Correct. Conditional update is not additionally required.
locked-recheck.cache: Faster reads and staleness even with TTL; never authorize from cache, locked DB recheck authoritative. Correct.

comparison.coverage: Both substantively cover the same four topics; no genuine omitted topic should be invented.
comparison.approach: Conditional update atomically tests/decrements positive remaining seats; other locks shared row then rereads/consumes capacity. Attribution must reverse correctly when target/peer swap.
comparison.shared: Both use atomic grouped transaction/rollback, unique student-course duplicate protection and DB-authoritative cache safety.
comparison.optional: TTL is explicit only in locked-recheck, but not mandatory and not evidence of a deficient alternative. No ranking/grades/plagiarism or code requirement.

privacy.public_rule: No author names, account IDs, Peer-1/Peer-2 labels, full other work or direct other-work quotations in public comparison text. Own-source evidence in individual feedback is allowed; private comparison evidence is Lecturer-only.
privacy.limits: Passing two synthetic canaries is narrow evidence, not general identity-inference protection.

review_method: Agent source/rubric review per claim; count required substantive versus optional wording edits, severity, false/missing findings and misattribution. No additional model judge or prompt tuning.
